newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS PRESS - AUG 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS PRESS - AUG 18.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- 500 JOBS AT 'SUPER-PIT' HANGING IN THE BALANCE

500 miners at the Asfordby deep mine in Leicestershire are waiting to see whether the pit - hailed in the 1980s as one of British Coal's new super-pits - is to be closed on economic and safety grounds. Crisis talks are due to be held Monday between management and miners' leaders after geological problems over viability and safety. Neil Greatorex, leader of the Union of Democratic Miners, has urged owners RJB Mining to give the mine more time.
-- PILLAR SELLS LEEDS STORE TO UNIT TRUST FOR 20M STG

Pillar Property has sold a freehold store and large shop at Briggate, Leeds, currently occupied by the Burton Group, to the Schroder Exempt Property Unit Trust. The total purchase price for the deal will be 20.75m stg when works are completed by the middle of next year.
-- EMU 'A WINNER FOR SPECULATORS'

Walter Eltis, a leading free market economist, has claimed that currency speculators such as George Soros will make massive profits out of European economic and monetary union. Writing in a pamphlet published by the Centre for Policy Studies, Eltis says that Emu is a 'colossal one-way bet' and that speculators cannot fail to make money.
THE TIMES
-- WORKERS' STAKE PLAN FOR POST OFFICE

The government is considering proposals to offer a form of employee ownership to workers in the state-owned postal service. The move, which would be supported by senior managers, would improve industrial relations at the Post Office and help avert a series of new strikes planned by workers this autumn. The Post Office has been beset by poor industrial relations over the last 18 months, and the move would also offer the service greater commercial freedom.
-- BT ATTEMPT TO CUT MCI PRICE 'LIKELY TO FAIL'

Audrey Mandela, international senior vice-president of US telecoms consulting and research firm Yankee Group, has stated any attempt by British Telecommunications to re-negotiate the terms of its 14bn stg deal with MCI will most likely fail. Mandela commented BT would have 'very little room for negotiation' within the deal, but she did see it as unlikely that the British company would abandon the arrangement altogether. BT has denied rumours that US phone company GTE was looking to replace it as MCI's partner.
-- BASS HAS HIT LIST OF POTENTIAL TAKEOVERS

Brewing and leisure group Bass has reportedly drafted a list of potential takeover candidates, which include William Hill, Stakis and First Leisure. The company is also looking to acquire additional European hotels so it can further plans to expand its Holiday Inn chain. Both Bass and First Leisure declined to comment on rumours the former was considering a 650m stg bid to acquire the latter.
THE GUARDIAN
-- EX-DIRECTORS OF BRITISH BIOTECH GAINED OVER 7M STG IN SHARE OPTIONS

According to British Biotech's annual report, three former directors at the UK pharmaceuticals group shared in over 7m stg in profits from exercising share options upon their departure. Former finance director James Noble received profits of 2.3m stg on top of an estimated 1.7m stg salary, while former commercial director Ronald Irwin received 2.4m stg and John Gordon gained 2.9m stg.
-- NATIONAL GRID PONDERS 1BN STG SALE OF ENERGIS

National Grid's Energis telecommunications is considering plans to float on the stock market before the end of the year, valuing it at about 1.7bn stg. Morgan Stanley telecoms analyst Paul Marsch said the float would enhance National Grid share prices, much as British Aerospace gained from the float of Orange. Energis is expected to report its first pre-tax profit this year, compared with a 14.4m stg loss in 1996/97.
-- LABOUR 'IGNORING MILLENNIUM BUG'

Taskforce 2000 head Robin Guenier has stated the government is doing very little to alert Britain of the dangers posed by the millennium bug, as they 'do not realise the scope of the problem'. Guenier warned hundreds of thousands of companies and public sector groups were unlikely to sort out the problem in time, which could lead to widespread chaos. Guenier has now asked for 3m stg to help warn the public, but the Department of Trade and Industry has stated he will get no more than 450,000 stg.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- RETAILERS AMONG RISING NUMBER OF INSOLVENCY CASES

The Society of Insolvency Practitioners along with the 'intensive care' departments from some of the largest high street banks have reported an increase in the number of companies coming on their books. Retailers and hi-tech companies have been the most prevalent, along with small and medium-sized companies who have experienced difficulties fulfilling market expectations. A corporate recovery partner from Arthur Anderson labelled the increase 'part of the economic cycle'.
-- JOB LOSSES EXPECTED AT LAURA ASHLEY

Struggling retailer Laura Ashley has announced it is to cut several hundred jobs at its manufacturing plants in Wales, where 900 are employed for the group's clothing and home furnishing divisions. The jobs are expected to be lost among the 500 working in garment manufacture. Laura Ashley will also issue a trading statement this week, which is expected to contain a warning on profits.
-- SUPERMARKETS SWEEP UP THE MUSIC CHARTS

A study from retail consultancy Verdict Research indicates supermarkets have increased their share of Britain's music market from three per cent in 1991 to 11 per cent last year. The supermarkets have not affected specialist megastores such as HMV and Virgin-Our Price, however, but have taken sales from multiple retailers such as Woolworths, WH Smith and John Menzies.
